chapter: Chicago, Villa Venice and Louis Armstrong
title: Sixty dollars a week and escorts through Capone territory
summary: The owner keeps the band at $60 and has armed men drive them through Capone's territory; later Teddy Wilson's car runs the north side.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: He said, "Now listen, you guys play the show better than anybody I've ever had here," and he says, "and you can play dance music." Now the job was paying us $60.00 a week a man.

He says, "Now if you want to stay here, and work, you got the job." He says, "I'm going to show you. I don't owe nobody." So number ten was saying that it was on forbidden territory, so $60.00 a week, we say, hell, we'll stay.

He says, "Well if you'll stay, I'll put my men in [el] to take you back to where you can catch the subway on the south side to go home." We had to go through Capone's territory, 'cause this was like on -- ten or twelve miles on the other side of (Nile Center), you know.
And every night they got us, we'd get into a car, with the submachine gun, and take us through the Capone territory. And then we would get on the elevated -- on the el.
On the el. The Chicago El.
Because it went as far as --
-- you know, forget the this stop, last stop, the last stop on the El, man, you know, and then we would go back.

Then finally, Teddy bought an old Chrysler car that we used to ride in there, and going through the north side we had to lock all of the doors, because those cats, they'd see a black person come through the north side, then, and you stopped for a light, and they'll snatch the door open and just beat the hell out of you for kicks.
